statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 8, low, for the 00:00Z hour. The Sunday reopen has now produced a genuine price path and it is orderly: Nasdaq-100 futures were verified at 29,471.50, up 83.75 points and 0.28%, at 23:49Z, and quoted at 29,446.75 inside a 29,423.75-29,470.25 session band at 00:14Z, roughly 80 points wide against a 29,388.50 reopen. S&P 500 futures were 7,700.00, up 0.11%, at 00:10Z inside a 7,681.50-7,703.25 range. That is a modest tech-led drift with two-way trade, not the persistent no-retracement structure that Tail measures, so Tail eases from 9 to 8. Stress is 39, moderate, down from 42: WTI has eased 1.25% to $85.98 and Brent 1.14% to $93.32, and VIX closed Friday at 14.89, down 6.00%, while long-end Treasury yields stay near multi-month highs with the 30-year at 5.23% and the 10-year at 4.69% on the 20 August H.15. Confidence is 85, high, on two independent live futures quotes, an official yield release, verified oil and volatility levels, complete cross-asset context and a verified calendar. The narrow 18:00Z-20:00Z danger window around the US Treasury news conference on new Iran sanctions is unchanged and Tail remains below the block threshold throughout the published path.
recommendation: The observed reopen path is consistent with functioning mean reversion. Over the first two and a half hours of the week Nasdaq-100 futures have traded an approximately 80-point band, about 0.28% of the index level, and are quoted in the upper part of it rather than extending away from it. There is no shallow-pullback sequence, no repeated extension after a failed retracement and no session-extreme holding on volume, which are the specific behaviours that have previously overwhelmed a reverse or grid approach. Cross-asset context agrees and is benign rather than aligned in a risk-off discontinuity: S&P futures up 0.11%, Dow futures up 0.02%, VIX futures down 0.3%, Treasury futures flat to 0.14% firmer and crude down about 1%. The exposures that remain are cross-asset and scheduled. Long-end yields near multi-month highs keep bond volatility the main transmission channel into Nasdaq, the 18:00Z US Treasury news conference on new Iran sanctions is the day's one high-impact catalyst, and Wednesday carries both the PCE, GDP and durable-goods stack at 12:30Z and Nvidia results after the close. Those raise Stress and shape the conditional path; none of them is observed price-path evidence today. Mapped policy state remains EA_ON with a narrow 18:00Z-20:00Z danger window.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures drift to 29,471.50, up 0.28%, inside an 80-point reopen band: Tail eases to 8, low, mapped policy state EA_ON, with conditional readings of 8 to 18 over the next twenty-three hours peaking at Monday's 18:00Z US Treasury news conference on new Iran sanctions.
body:
Two and a half hours into the Globex week the Sunday reopen has resolved into a contained, mildly firm price path. Nasdaq-100 futures were verified at 29,471.50, up 83.75 points and 0.28%, at 23:49Z, and a second independent source quoted 29,446.75, up 59.00 and 0.20%, inside a 29,423.75-29,470.25 band at 00:14Z. Against the 29,388.50 reopen print that is a drift of roughly 60 to 85 points inside a band about 80 points wide. S&P 500 futures were 7,700.00, up 8.75 and 0.11%, at 00:10Z within a 7,681.50-7,703.25 range. The cross-index spread is small and tech-led, which is a normal leadership pattern rather than a dislocation.

Delayed cross-asset context is consistent: Nasdaq futures 0.27%, S&P futures 0.12%, Dow futures 0.02%, VIX futures -0.3%, gold -0.14%, and two-, five-, ten- and thirty-year Treasury futures flat to 0.14% firmer, so the marginal overnight move in duration is a small yield relief rather than another leg higher. Crude has eased: WTI is $85.98, down 1.25%, and Brent $93.32, down 1.14%, with Reuters reporting profit-taking ahead of the Treasury announcement. VIX closed Friday at 14.89, down 6.00%, a subdued level that sits awkwardly with the size of the week's scheduled calendar and is one reason Stress stays in the moderate band rather than falling further.

The macro backdrop is unchanged and is where the residual risk sits. The 20 August H.15 release puts the 2-year at 4.19%, the 10-year at 4.69% and the 30-year at 5.23%, with the long end near multi-month highs after bond volatility drove last week's Nasdaq weakness. Two weekend catalysts, the new US 50% tariffs on roughly $20bn of Canadian goods and Canada's matching retaliation from 8 September, have now been through a full reopen without index-level repricing. The live technology narrative is Alibaba's HK$80bn, $10.2bn, Hong Kong share placement announced on 23 August, with all net proceeds directed at full-stack AI capability including chips and infrastructure, which supports the AI-capex theme into Nvidia's results on Wednesday.

Friday's internals were split rather than aligned, which argues against a one-way regime: application and infrastructure software rose 1.18% and 1.15% and communication services 0.92%, while semiconductors fell 0.31% with ARM down 2.95% and Intel down 2.24%. Megacaps were five up and three down, led by Tesla at 5.14% and Alphabet at 1.22% against Nvidia at -0.98% and Apple at -0.63%. Conflicting internals of that kind normally reduce directional conviction rather than raise Tail.

The published path therefore keeps Tail low through the Asian and European sessions, steps modestly for the European cash open at 07:00Z and the US cash open inside the 13:00Z hour, where opening-auction continuation is the specific pattern that has previously denied mean reversion, and peaks at 18 for the two hours covering the 18:00Z US Treasury news conference on new Iran sanctions and any delayed second leg. Every published hour stays below the block threshold. Later in the week the PCE, GDP and durable-goods stack at 12:30Z on 26 August, Nvidia results after that day's close, and the Jackson Hole keynote by Fed Chair Warsh at 14:00Z on 28 August are the scheduled items most capable of changing this assessment.

lookbackSummary: Claude coverage over the past twenty-four hours is nearly complete: twenty hourly assessments are available and four clock-hours are marked unavailable, at 07:00Z, 10:00Z, 11:00Z and 12:00Z on 23 August. Tail held 4 through every hour of the weekend futures halt, when no Nasdaq-100 price path could develop at all, stepped to 15 in the 22:00Z reopen hour to cover the still-unpriced weekend queue, then fell back to 9 at 23:00Z once the reopen printed without a gap. The mapped policy state stayed EA_ON and the dominant mode remained normal in every available hour, so no hour approached the block threshold. Stress traced a full weekend arc: 38 at the start of the window, a low of 34 through the European morning and early afternoon, then a steady climb across the evening to 45 in the last three pre-reopen hours as the Canadian tariff escalation and Monday's scheduled Iran announcement accumulated, before easing to 42 once the reopen cleared. Confidence sat between 82 and 87 throughout, dipping to its low of 82 in the reopen hour when the first live print was still incomplete and recovering to 86 immediately afterwards.
outlookSummary: The current hour carries Tail 8 and Stress 39 on an observed and contained reopen path rather than on assumption, because two independent verified Nasdaq-100 futures quotes now exist for the slot and they agree. Conditional Tail then holds a floor of 8 through the Asian session, where two-way trade has historically been most reliable and no US release is scheduled, while Stress decays to 36 as the weekend risk premium finishes unwinding. Tail steps to 10 for the European pre-open and 12 at the 07:00Z European cash open, the first substantial liquidity event and the point at which any overnight drift is confirmed or faded, then eases again through a quiet European late morning. The 12:30Z Chicago Fed National Activity Index is treated as a checkpoint at Tail 11 rather than a step, because it is a medium-impact composite. The US cash open inside the 13:00Z hour carries 15 for opening-auction continuation risk, easing to 14 and 12 across the auction window and to 11 in the midday lull. The path peaks at 18 with Stress 49 and mode event/whipsaw for the 18:00Z and 19:00Z hours around the US Treasury news conference on new Iran sanctions, covering both the initial repricing and a delayed second leg, then eases to 14 into the 20:00Z cash close and to 8 in the 21:00Z Globex maintenance halt. The 22:00Z reopen carries 9 for gap risk on any headline landing inside the halt. Every published hour remains below the block threshold, and Confidence decays from 85 to 62 across the window in line with forecast distance.
